title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
abstract: Hands-on workshop building a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. Profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. End with a hybrid deployment and a live cost dashboard showing 30-45% savings vs GPU-only baselines.

title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of CMP323-R. Hybrid CPU/GPU multi-agent system on EC2 with routing policies and a live cost dashboard showing 30-45% savings vs GPU-only.

title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
abstract: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver price-performance for inference and select training. Breaks down where G7e/G7 fits: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS/$) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. Covers the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), a TCO comparison, and a decision framework for G7e/G7 vs P-family.

title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
abstract: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. AWS and OpenAI share scheduling and bin-packing strategies for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers: rack-aware placement respecting 72-GPU NVLink domains, mixed workload profiles (prefill vs decode vs batch), capacity block utilization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints.

title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, GPUs that pass health checks yet corrupt results. Diagnose these on NVIDIA GPU-based EC2 with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against baselines, run open-source health checks. Leave with a failure-signature runbook.

title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. Match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Decision framework covering instance types, DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration with Research and Engineering Studio (RES). video-games lens: VFX render farm artist desktops.

title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
abstract: Organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU families. Scaling Spot requires understanding how capacity behaves. The EC2 Spot product leader shares which diversification strategies deliver high fill rates, how allocation differs for CPU vs GPU, when Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager matter. A playbook on instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ, checkpointing, and capacity rebalancing.

title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
abstract: You have enough GPUs to cover your software requirements, but is that all you need? Picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes at scale. Lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately, how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and using AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. A cloud and bare-metal architectural pattern plus a GPU selection framework.

title: GPU orchestration at scale using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
abstract: Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unsharable integers. Deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision an EKS cluster with NVIDIA L4 nodes, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the adapter with vLLM, comparing base vs fine-tuned responses in real time. ai+nvidia lens: pairs with the QLoRA pipeline work.

title: GPU orchestration at scale using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of HMC401-R. NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS, Terraform-provisioned L4 nodes, QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-14B served with vLLM.

title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
abstract: SageMaker HyperPod as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. How customers maximize GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and teams with shared architectures. SageMaker Studio for iteration on the shared pool. Humain's optimization across two large HyperPod clusters with team isolation and advanced task submission.

title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
abstract: GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. Storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference. How Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.

title: Accelerate AI workloads with GPUs on Amazon ECS Managed Instances
abstract: Running GPU workloads in containers means choosing the right accelerator, right-sizing instances, and scaling without over-provisioning. Amazon ECS Managed Instances handles infrastructure lifecycle while giving access to the latest GPUs. Launch GPU capacity with managed provisioning, scale on real GPU metrics rather than CPU proxies, recover from hardware failures. Ramp built and scaled production AI infrastructure on ECS Managed Instances.

title: Accelerating Data Processing: GPU Accelerated Amazon EMR at the Enterprise Scale
abstract: As AI agents ask increasingly complex questions, analytics systems must become more responsive over hundreds of terabytes and trillions of rows. GPU acceleration integrated with Amazon EMR improves performance and efficiency, with the NVIDIA cuDF Router enabling seamless migration across a large enterprise. The smart router continuously directs workloads for better performance and cost efficiency.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte weights through storage->network->CPU->PCIe->GPU. Benchmarks four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI lazy-loading, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU. When each shines, how they compose, tradeoffs optimizing inference cold starts on EKS. kro and ACK for declarative provisioning.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of OPN403-R. Benchmarks SOCI, s5cmd, Mountpoint S3 CSI, and Run.ai Model Streamer for accelerating model delivery to GPU memory; kro and ACK for declarative storage pipelines on EKS.

title: Stop paying for idle GPUs on Amazon EKS (sponsored by Apptio)
abstract: AI workloads can consume millions in infrastructure before anyone notices whether they're used efficiently. GPUs sit idle, clusters become overprovisioned. How EKS teams identify wasted GPU capacity, understand true cost of AI workloads, and automate optimization without sacrificing performance.

title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. Why NUMA matters for memory locality running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate thread-to-data alignment, especially as SIMD and AMX amplify memory bandwidth demands. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Distinguished (500) level.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2
abstract: AI agents write, execute, and iterate on code autonomously. Every session needs an isolated sandbox to run untrusted code safely. How customers deploy agent sandboxes on EC2 across distinct patterns, each trading off isolation, latency, and performance across instance families. Isolation trade-offs, cost per sandbox-second, capacity planning at scale. A decision model for selecting the right pattern. favorites lens: directly relevant to the microvm/firecracker sandbox work.

title: Deploy AI agent sandboxes on EC2 [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of CMP328-R. AI agent sandboxes on EC2: isolation patterns, cost per sandbox-second, capacity planning, decision model.

title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
abstract: SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep through distributed training to deployment, on one self-healing platform. Tencent Games, a game AI team not an infra team, went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Lessons on EFA networking, FSx storage, GPU fault tolerance. video-games lens: game AI at production scale.

title: How Prime Video Built an AI-assisted Creative Suite on AWS
abstract: Premium animated series traditionally take 3.5 years to produce. Prime Video AI Studios built the AI-Assisted Creative Suite on AWS to compress production to under 12 months, extending to live-action shorts, second-unit VFX, feature films. Powered by AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Strands that select models, build creative workflows, construct prompts, evaluate outputs. Trains and serves a first-party diffusion-model fleet on SageMaker and EKS on EC2 P6 GPU clusters. video-games lens: creative/animation AI pipeline.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
abstract: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI. Two CPU-intensive patterns on EC2: AI inference (serving LM predictions at scale on Graviton and x86, with cost/latency tradeoffs) and agentic AI (sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, interact with external systems, needing fast isolated ephemeral compute). Production architectures, benchmarks across instance families, a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2 [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of CMP333-R. CPU roles in production AI: inference on Graviton/x86 and agentic sandboxes; benchmarks and a decision framework for AI beyond GPUs.

title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
abstract: How Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed, not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one including Amazon can access unencrypted data. NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs, mutual TLS with embedded attestation, key lifecycle within encrypted VM memory. favorites lens: Bee is the ambient-audio source in ARC324; zero-trust personal AI is squarely bryan's interest.

title: Agents at the Gate: Governing AI in EC2 Image Builder
abstract: EC2 Image Builder pipelines sprawl fast, and frontier agents that run for hours unattended need guardrails. Decompose Image Builder operations into reusable agent skills run via Kiro, Claude Code. Author AWSTOE components and orchestrate workflows, harden images, scan for CVEs. Mid-build, a WaitForAction step pauses the pipeline and hands the image to AWS Security Agent to pentest; findings decide whether the build ships, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval. favorites lens: Kiro agent skills + governance gate, directly the haunting pattern.

title: Agents at the Gate: Governing AI in EC2 Image Builder [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of CMP302-R. Kiro-run agent skills for EC2 Image Builder with a WaitForAction pentest gate via AWS Security Agent, bounded by severity, iteration caps, and human approval.

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, survive failures that compound with scale. Walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based EC2 instances, compute/network/storage, ML stack from drivers to distributed frameworks, and stand up observability from GPU/EFA/Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. Leave with dashboards you built and a goodput methodology.

title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive [REPEAT]
abstract: Repeat of AIM347-R. Full-stack GPU cluster performance engineering on Slurm-managed NVIDIA EC2: profiling, collectives, observability from GPU/EFA/Lustre counters to MFU and goodput.

title: Make AMD Your Default on AWS: Efficient EC2 for the Agentic AI Era with EPYC (sponsored by AMD)
abstract: Run agentic AI for over 30% less on Amazon EC2 within existing contracts. As autonomous agents call inference models and tools, compute demand explodes and the CPU-to-GPU ratio inverts from 1:8 to 8:1, making processor choice the defining ROI decision. 5th-Gen AMD EPYC Turin on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, >30% OpEx savings redirectable into AI budgets.

title: 50k daily iOS builds with virtualization on Amazon EC2 Mac
abstract: An automotive manufacturer migrated CI/CD from on-prem to AWS for 130,000+ daily builds (50k+ iOS) across 1,300+ microservices. Amazon EC2 Mac instances with virtualization using Tart enable ephemeral macOS VMs booting in seconds with pre-configured toolchains. Build times dropped 90 to 35 minutes, a 61% improvement, scaling to 50,000+ daily iOS builds for 3,000+ developers.

title: EC2 instances from launch to fleet orchestration
abstract: Amazon EC2 offers over 1,000 instance types, five purchasing models, and a growing set of fleet and capacity tools. A comprehensive guide: the full EC2 portfolio from Graviton5 to accelerated instances, On-Demand/Spot/Savings Plans/Capacity Reservations, and how EC2 Fleet, Auto Scaling, and Capacity Manager help run the right instances at the right price.

title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
abstract: Amazon EC2 continues to push cloud compute boundaries: new AWS Graviton processors and the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances. How customers use EC2 to accelerate application development, HPC, and AI inference on the CPU. The AWS Nitro System for isolation and performance, plus guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.
